## File overview

The purpose of this file is to further investigate the rank ordering of
pathogen prevalence for the EcoMiD cohort, both by IgG and PCR.

|     |
|-----|

## System setup

```{r}
# Read in files 
library(here)
source(here("R", "0-config.R"))
```

## Read in files

```{r}
# seropositivity individual level
# seroconversion by community type + pathogen
sero_inc_type <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_pathogen_comm_sero_inc_3_levels.rds"))  %>% 
  filter(pathogen != "Strongyloides" & pathogen != "T. solium")
sero_inc_type$community_type2 <- factor(sero_inc_type$community_type2, levels = c("Esmeraldas", "Borbon", "Rural"))

# seroprevalence by community type + pathogen
sero_prev_type <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_sero_prev_rates_3_levels.rds"))
sero_prev_type$community_type2 <- factor(sero_prev_type$community_type2, levels = c("Esmeraldas", "Borbon", "Rural"))

# pcr prevalence by community type + pathogen
pcr_prev_type <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_pcr_prev_by_community_3_levels.rds"))
pcr_prev_type$community_type2 <- factor(pcr_prev_type$community_type2, levels = c("Esmeraldas", "Borbon", "Rural"))

# seroreversion rate by community type + pathogen 
sero_rev_type <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_pathogen_comm_sero_rev_3_levels.rds")) %>% 
  filter(pathogen != "Strongyloides" & pathogen != "T. solium")
sero_rev_type$community_type2 <- factor(sero_rev_type$community_type2, levels = c("Esmeraldas", "Borbon", "Rural"))

# overall measures (by pathogen)
sero_prev_path <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_sero_prev_rates.rds")) %>% 
  filter(community_name == "All communities")

pcr_prev_path <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_pcr_prev_by_pathogen.rds"))

# seroincidence 

sero_inc_path <- readRDS(here("output/ecomid_pathogen_sero_inc.rds")) %>% 
  filter(pathogen != "Strongyloides" & pathogen != "T. solium")

```

## Assay rank ordering

### 1a) Overall pathogen prevalence

```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## Rank order of pathogen prevalence: IgG vs. PCR (slope/bump chart)
## Inputs: pcr_prev_path (pathogen, prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci)
##         sero_prev_path (pathogen, sero_prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci)
## (sero_prev_path is labeled "IgG" throughout figures/tables)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Keep only pathogens present in BOTH dataframes, then rank within
##    each assay (rank 1 = highest prevalence) ----
shared_pathogens <- intersect(pcr_prev_path$pathogen, sero_prev_path$pathogen)

pcr_rank <- pcr_prev_path %>%
  filter(pathogen %in% shared_pathogens) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, assay = "PCR", prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min"))

sero_rank <- sero_prev_path %>%
  filter(pathogen %in% shared_pathogens) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, assay = "IgG",
            prevalence = sero_prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min"))

rank_df <- bind_rows(pcr_rank, sero_rank) %>%
  mutate(assay = factor(assay, levels = c("IgG", "PCR")))

## 2. Slope/bump chart ---------------------------------------------------
n_pathogens <- n_distinct(rank_df$pathogen)

p <- ggplot(rank_df, aes(x = assay, y = rank, group = pathogen)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = pathogen), linewidth = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = pathogen), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df, assay == "IgG"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 0.85, hjust = 1, size = 3.3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df, assay == "PCR"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 2.15, hjust = 0, size = 3.3
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_len(n_pathogens)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.9, 0.9))) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Rank (1 = highest prevalence)",
    title = "Rank order of pathogen prevalence: IgG vs. PCR"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

## Swap in your lab theme here, e.g.:
## p <- p + your_lab_theme() + scale_color_manual(values = your_palette)

print(p)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_slopechart.png", p, width = 7, height = 0.4 * n_pathogens + 2, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Companion dumbbell plot with 95% CIs, ordered by mean rank
##    (useful if you also want to show precision, not just order)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

order_df <- rank_df %>%
  group_by(pathogen) %>%
  summarize(mean_rank = mean(rank), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(mean_rank)

rank_df2 <- rank_df %>%
  mutate(pathogen = factor(pathogen, levels = rev(order_df$pathogen)))

p2 <- ggplot(rank_df2, aes(x = prevalence, y = pathogen, color = assay)) +
geom_line(aes(group = pathogen), color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6) +
geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
height = 0.15, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
scale_color_manual(values = c(PCR = "#009E73", IgG = "#CC79A7")) +
labs(
x = "Prevalence", y = NULL, color = "Assay",
title = "Pathogen prevalence by assay (ranked, with 95% CI)"
) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

print(p2)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Wide-format data (one row per pathogen) used by the scatter
##    plot and table below
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

wide_rank <- sero_rank %>%
  select(pathogen, igg_prevalence = prevalence, igg_lower = lower_ci,
         igg_upper = upper_ci, igg_rank = rank) %>%
  inner_join(
    pcr_rank %>%
      select(pathogen, pcr_prevalence = prevalence, pcr_lower = lower_ci,
             pcr_upper = upper_ci, pcr_rank = rank),
    by = "pathogen"
  ) %>%
  mutate(rank_diff = igg_rank - pcr_rank) %>%
  arrange(igg_rank)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Rank-rank scatter plot (concordance between assays)
##    Points on the dashed diagonal = same rank in both assays;
##    the further off the diagonal, the more the assays disagree.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

# install.packages("ggrepel") if not already installed
library(ggrepel)

p3 <- ggplot(wide_rank, aes(x = igg_rank, y = pcr_rank)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = pathogen), size = 3.3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(n_pathogens)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_len(n_pathogens)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "IgG rank", y = "PCR rank") + 
    #title = "Concordance of pathogen rank between IgG and PCR"
  #) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

print(p3)
#ggsave(here("figures/suppfig9_concordance_path_rank_all.png"), p3, height = 7, width = 7)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Summary table (pathogen, prevalence + 95% CI, and rank, by assay)
##    A table is a good complement here: the charts show pattern/order
##    at a glance, but a table gives exact numbers reviewers/collaborators
##    may want (and is easy to drop into a manuscript supplement).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

# install.packages("gt") if not already installed
library(gt)

# NOTE: assumes prevalence/CI columns are proportions (0-1); if they are
# already percentages, drop the "* 100" below.
table_df <- wide_rank %>%
  mutate(
    IgG = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", igg_prevalence * 100, igg_lower * 100, igg_upper * 100),
    PCR = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", pcr_prevalence * 100, pcr_lower * 100, pcr_upper * 100)
  ) %>%
  select(pathogen, IgG, igg_rank, PCR, pcr_rank, rank_diff)

gt_tbl <- table_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Pathogen prevalence and rank order by assay") %>%
  cols_label(
    pathogen = "Pathogen",
    IgG = "IgG prevalence (95% CI)",
    igg_rank = "IgG rank",
    PCR = "PCR prevalence (95% CI)",
    pcr_rank = "PCR rank",
    rank_diff = "Rank Δ (IgG − PCR)"
  ) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(igg_rank, pcr_rank, rank_diff)) %>%
  opt_row_striping()

gt_tbl

## Optional: save table as image/html
## gtsave(gt_tbl, "pathogen_prevalence_table.png")


```

### 1b) Prevalence by community type

```{r}

## 1. Keep only pathogen x community_type2 combinations present in BOTH
##    dataframes, then rank within each assay x community_type2 group
##    (rank 1 = highest prevalence) ----

common_combos <- inner_join(
  pcr_prev_type %>% distinct(pathogen, community_type2),
  sero_prev_type %>% distinct(pathogen, community_type2),
  by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")
)

## Relabel community_type2 values for display

pcr_rank <- pcr_prev_type %>%
  semi_join(common_combos, by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, community_type2,
            assay = "PCR", prevalence = pcr_prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci) %>%
  group_by(community_type2) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min")) %>%
  ungroup()

sero_rank <- sero_prev_type %>%
  semi_join(common_combos, by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, community_type2,
            assay = "IgG", prevalence = sero_prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci) %>%
  group_by(community_type2) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min")) %>%
  ungroup()

rank_df <- bind_rows(sero_rank, pcr_rank) %>%
  mutate(assay = factor(assay, levels = c("IgG", "PCR")))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Faceted slope/bump chart: IgG vs. PCR rank, one panel per
##    community type (comparison A)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p1 <- ggplot(rank_df, aes(x = assay, y = rank, group = pathogen)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = pathogen), linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = pathogen), size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df, assay == "IgG"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 0.8, hjust = 1, size = 2.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df, assay == "PCR"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 2.2, hjust = 0, size = 2.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~community_type2, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(1.1, 1.1))) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Rank (1 = highest prevalence)",
    title = "Rank order of pathogen prevalence, IgG vs. PCR, by community type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p1)

## Swap in your lab theme here, e.g.:
## p1 <- p1 + your_lab_theme() + scale_color_manual(values = your_palette)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_by_community_type_slope.png", p1, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Bump chart across community types, faceted by assay
##    (comparison B: does rank order shift across community types,
##    and is that shift similar for IgG and PCR?)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Label pathogens at the last community type on the x-axis
last_ct <- rank_df %>%
  distinct(community_type2) %>%
  pull(community_type2) %>%
  sort() %>%
  tail(1)

label_df <- filter(rank_df, community_type2 == last_ct)

p2 <- ggplot(rank_df, aes(x = community_type2, y = rank, group = pathogen, color = pathogen)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = label_df, aes(label = pathogen),
    direction = "y", hjust = 0, xlim = c(NA, NA), size = 2.8, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~assay, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Community type", y = "Rank (1 = highest prevalence)",
    title = "Pathogen rank order across community types, by assay"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p2)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_across_community_type_bump.png", p2, width = 8, height = 9, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Compact alternative: rank heatmap (pathogen x community type,
##    faceted by assay) -- useful if there are many pathogens/community
##    types and the bump chart gets too busy to read
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p3 <- rank_df %>%
  mutate(pathogen = fct_reorder(pathogen, rank, .fun = mean)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = community_type2, y = pathogen, fill = rank)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = rank), size = 3, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~assay) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = -1, name = "Rank") +
  labs(
    x = "Community type", y = NULL,
    title = "Pathogen rank heatmap by community type and assay"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p3)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Wide-format data (one row per pathogen x community type) for
##    the table below
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

wide_rank <- sero_rank %>%
  select(pathogen, community_type2, igg_prevalence = prevalence,
         igg_lower = lower_ci, igg_upper = upper_ci, igg_rank = rank) %>%
  inner_join(
    pcr_rank %>%
      select(pathogen, community_type2, pcr_prevalence = prevalence,
             pcr_lower = lower_ci, pcr_upper = upper_ci, pcr_rank = rank),
    by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")
  ) %>%
  mutate(rank_diff = igg_rank - pcr_rank) %>%
  arrange(community_type2, igg_rank)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Rank-rank scatter plot (concordance between assays), colored by
##    community type -- same idea as the aggregate version, but here
##    every point is one pathogen x community-type combination
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p4 <- ggplot(wide_rank, aes(x = igg_rank, y = pcr_rank, color = community_type2)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = pathogen), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = nytpal) +
  labs(
    x = "IgG rank", y = "PCR rank", color = NULL,
    title = "Concordance of pathogen rank between IgG and PCR, by community type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p4)

## If labels get too cluttered with many pathogens/community types, try
## faceting instead of coloring:
## p4 + facet_wrap(~community_type2)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_scatter_by_community_type.png", p4, width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Summary table, grouped by community type
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

# NOTE: assumes prevalence/CI columns are proportions (0-1); if they are
# already percentages, drop the "* 100" below.
table_df <- wide_rank %>%
  mutate(
    IgG = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", igg_prevalence * 100, igg_lower * 100, igg_upper * 100),
    PCR = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", pcr_prevalence * 100, pcr_lower * 100, pcr_upper * 100)
  ) %>%
  select(community_type2, pathogen, IgG, igg_rank, PCR, pcr_rank, rank_diff)

gt_tbl <- table_df %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "community_type2") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Pathogen prevalence and rank order by assay and community type") %>%
  cols_label(
    pathogen = "Pathogen",
    IgG = "IgG prevalence (95% CI)",
    igg_rank = "IgG rank",
    PCR = "PCR prevalence (95% CI)",
    pcr_rank = "PCR rank",
    rank_diff = "Rank Δ (IgG − PCR)"
  ) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(igg_rank, pcr_rank, rank_diff)) %>%
  opt_row_striping()

gt_tbl <- gt_tbl %>% as.data.frame()
gt_tbl
## Optional: save table as image/html
write_xlsx(gt_tbl, here("output/supp_pathogen_prevalence_table_by_community_type.xlsx"))

```

## Seroconversion rank ordering

### 2a) Overall seroconversion rate vs. PCR prevalence

```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## Rank order of pathogen seroconversion rate (IgG) vs. PCR prevalence
## Inputs: pcr_prev_path (pathogen, prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci)
##         sero_inc_path (pathogen, ir_per_100, ir_lo_per_100, ir_hi_per_100)
## (sero_inc_path is labeled "IgG SCR" throughout figures/tables; SCR =
## seroconversion rate, per 100 person-years)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Keep only pathogens present in BOTH dataframes, then rank within
##    each assay (rank 1 = highest rate/prevalence) ----
shared_pathogens_sc <- intersect(pcr_prev_path$pathogen, sero_inc_path$pathogen)

pcr_rank_sc <- pcr_prev_path %>%
  filter(pathogen %in% shared_pathogens_sc) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, assay = "PCR", prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min"))

sero_inc_rank <- sero_inc_path %>%
  filter(pathogen %in% shared_pathogens_sc) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, assay = "IgG SCR",
            prevalence = ir_obs_per_100, lower_ci = ir_lo_per_100, upper_ci = ir_hi_per_100) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min"))

rank_df_sc <- bind_rows(sero_inc_rank, pcr_rank_sc) %>%
  mutate(assay = factor(assay, levels = c("IgG SCR", "PCR")))

## 2. Slope/bump chart ---------------------------------------------------
n_pathogens_sc <- n_distinct(rank_df_sc$pathogen)

p5 <- ggplot(rank_df_sc, aes(x = assay, y = rank, group = pathogen)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = pathogen), linewidth = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = pathogen), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df_sc, assay == "IgG SCR"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 0.85, hjust = 1, size = 3.3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df_sc, assay == "PCR"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 2.15, hjust = 0, size = 3.3
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_len(n_pathogens_sc)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.9, 0.9))) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Rank (1 = highest rate/prevalence)",
    title = "Rank order of pathogen seroconversion rate (IgG) vs. PCR prevalence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p5)

## Swap in your lab theme here, e.g.:
## p5 <- p5 + your_lab_theme() + scale_color_manual(values = your_palette)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_scr_slopechart.png", p5, width = 7, height = 0.4 * n_pathogens_sc + 2, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Companion dumbbell plot with 95% CIs, ordered by mean rank
##    NOTE: IgG SCR is a rate per 100 person-years and PCR prevalence
##    is a proportion -- different units plotted on one x-axis so the
##    ranks/CIs sit side by side. If the mixed units are misleading,
##    consider faceting by assay with independent x-scales instead.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

order_df_sc <- rank_df_sc %>%
  group_by(pathogen) %>%
  summarize(mean_rank = mean(rank), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(mean_rank)

rank_df_sc2 <- rank_df_sc %>%
  mutate(pathogen = factor(pathogen, levels = rev(order_df_sc$pathogen)))

p6 <- ggplot(rank_df_sc2, aes(x = prevalence, y = pathogen, color = assay)) +
geom_line(aes(group = pathogen), color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6) +
geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
height = 0.15, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
scale_color_manual(values = c(PCR = "#009E73", `IgG SCR` = "#CC79A7")) +
labs(
x = "PCR prevalence / IgG seroconversion rate (per 100 py)", y = NULL, color = "Assay",
title = "Pathogen seroconversion rate (IgG) and PCR prevalence (ranked, with 95% CI)"
) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

print(p6)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Wide-format data (one row per pathogen) used by the scatter
##    plot and table below
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

wide_rank_sc <- sero_inc_rank %>%
  select(pathogen, igg_scr = prevalence, igg_scr_lower = lower_ci,
         igg_scr_upper = upper_ci, igg_rank = rank) %>%
  inner_join(
    pcr_rank_sc %>%
      select(pathogen, pcr_prevalence = prevalence, pcr_lower = lower_ci,
             pcr_upper = upper_ci, pcr_rank = rank),
    by = "pathogen"
  ) %>%
  mutate(rank_diff = igg_rank - pcr_rank) %>%
  arrange(igg_rank)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Rank-rank scatter plot (concordance between assays)
##    Points on the dashed diagonal = same rank in both assays;
##    the further off the diagonal, the more the assays disagree.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p7 <- ggplot(wide_rank_sc, aes(x = pcr_rank, y = igg_rank)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = pathogen), size = 3.3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_x_reverse(breaks = seq_len(n_pathogens_sc)) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_len(n_pathogens_sc)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    y = "IgG seroconversion rate rank", x = "PCR prevalence rank") +
    #title = "Concordance of pathogen rank between IgG seroconversion rate and PCR prevalence"
  #) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

print(p7)
ggsave(here("figures/suppfig9_concordance_path_rank_scr_all.tiff"), p7, width = 250, height = 190, units = "mm")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Summary table (pathogen, prevalence/rate + 95% CI, and rank,
##    by assay)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

# NOTE: PCR columns assume prevalence/CI are proportions (0-1); if they
# are already percentages, drop the "* 100" below. IgG SCR is assumed to
# already be on the "per 100 person-years" scale (ir_per_100 etc.).
table_df_sc <- wide_rank_sc %>%
  mutate(
    `IgG SCR (per 100 py)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)", igg_scr, igg_scr_lower, igg_scr_upper),
    PCR = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f–%.1f%%)", pcr_prevalence * 100, pcr_lower * 100, pcr_upper * 100)
  ) %>%
  select(pathogen, `IgG SCR (per 100 py)`, igg_rank, PCR, pcr_rank, rank_diff)

gt_tbl_sc <- table_df_sc %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Pathogen seroconversion rate (IgG) and PCR prevalence, ranked") %>%
  cols_label(
    pathogen = "Pathogen",
    igg_rank = "IgG SCR rank",
    pcr_rank = "PCR rank",
    rank_diff = "Rank Δ (IgG − PCR)"
  ) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(igg_rank, pcr_rank, rank_diff)) %>%
  opt_row_striping()

gt_tbl_sc

## Optional: save table as image/html
## gtsave(gt_tbl_sc, "pathogen_seroconversion_pcr_table.png")


```

### 2b) Seroconversion rate by community type vs. PCR prevalence

```{r}

## 1. Keep only pathogen x community_type2 combinations present in BOTH
##    dataframes, then rank within each assay x community_type2 group
##    (rank 1 = highest rate/prevalence) ----

common_combos_sc <- inner_join(
  pcr_prev_type %>% distinct(pathogen, community_type2),
  sero_inc_type %>% distinct(pathogen, community_type2),
  by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")
)

pcr_rank_sc_ct <- pcr_prev_type %>%
  semi_join(common_combos_sc, by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, community_type2,
            assay = "PCR", prevalence = pcr_prevalence, lower_ci, upper_ci) %>%
  group_by(community_type2) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min")) %>%
  ungroup()

sero_inc_rank_ct <- sero_inc_type %>%
  semi_join(common_combos_sc, by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")) %>%
  transmute(pathogen, community_type2,
            assay = "IgG SCR", prevalence = ir_per_100,
            lower_ci = ir_lo_per_100, upper_ci = ir_hi_per_100) %>%
  group_by(community_type2) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-prevalence, ties.method = "min")) %>%
  ungroup()

rank_df_sc_ct <- bind_rows(sero_inc_rank_ct, pcr_rank_sc_ct) %>%
  mutate(assay = factor(assay, levels = c("IgG SCR", "PCR")))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Faceted slope/bump chart: IgG SCR vs. PCR rank, one panel per
##    community type
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p8 <- ggplot(rank_df_sc_ct, aes(x = assay, y = rank, group = pathogen)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = pathogen), linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = pathogen), size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df_sc_ct, assay == "IgG SCR"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 0.8, hjust = 1, size = 2.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(rank_df_sc_ct, assay == "PCR"),
    aes(label = pathogen), x = 2.2, hjust = 0, size = 2.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~community_type2, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(1.1, 1.1))) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Rank (1 = highest rate/prevalence)",
    title = "Rank order of seroconversion rate (IgG) vs. PCR prevalence, by community type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p8)

## Swap in your lab theme here, e.g.:
## p8 <- p8 + your_lab_theme() + scale_color_manual(values = your_palette)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_scr_by_community_type_slope.png", p8, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Bump chart across community types, faceted by assay
##    (does rank order shift across community types, and is that
##    shift similar for IgG SCR and PCR?)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

last_ct_sc <- rank_df_sc_ct %>%
  distinct(community_type2) %>%
  pull(community_type2) %>%
  sort() %>%
  tail(1)

label_df_sc <- filter(rank_df_sc_ct, community_type2 == last_ct_sc)

p9 <- ggplot(rank_df_sc_ct, aes(x = community_type2, y = rank, group = pathogen, color = pathogen)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = label_df_sc, aes(label = pathogen),
    direction = "y", hjust = 0, xlim = c(NA, NA), size = 2.8, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~assay, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Community type", y = "Rank (1 = highest rate/prevalence)",
    title = "Pathogen rank order across community types: seroconversion rate (IgG) vs. PCR prevalence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p9)

## Optional: save
## ggsave("pathogen_rank_scr_across_community_type_bump.png", p9, width = 8, height = 9, dpi = 300)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Compact alternative: rank heatmap (pathogen x community type,
##    faceted by assay)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p10 <- rank_df_sc_ct %>%
  mutate(pathogen = fct_reorder(pathogen, rank, .fun = mean)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = community_type2, y = pathogen, fill = rank)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = rank), size = 3, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~assay) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = -1, name = "Rank") +
  labs(
    x = "Community type", y = NULL,
    title = "Pathogen rank heatmap by community type: seroconversion rate (IgG) vs. PCR prevalence"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

print(p10)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Wide-format data (one row per pathogen x community type) for
##    the table below
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

wide_rank_sc_ct <- sero_inc_rank_ct %>%
  select(pathogen, community_type2, igg_scr = prevalence,
         igg_scr_lower = lower_ci, igg_scr_upper = upper_ci, igg_rank = rank) %>%
  inner_join(
    pcr_rank_sc_ct %>%
      select(pathogen, community_type2, pcr_prevalence = prevalence,
             pcr_lower = lower_ci, pcr_upper = upper_ci, pcr_rank = rank),
    by = c("pathogen", "community_type2")
  ) %>%
  mutate(rank_diff = igg_rank - pcr_rank) %>%
  arrange(community_type2, pcr_rank)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Rank-rank scatter plot (concordance between assays), colored by
##    community type
## ---------------------------------------------------------------

p11 <- ggplot(wide_rank_sc_ct, aes(x = pcr_rank, y = igg_rank, color = community_type2)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = pathogen), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = breaks_width(1)) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = nytpal) +
  labs(
    x = "IgG seroconversion rate rank", y = "PCR prevalence rank", color = NULL,
    title = "Concordance of pathogen rank: seroconversion rate (IgG) vs. PCR prevalence, by community type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p11)

    `IgG SCR (per 100 py)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)", igg_scr, igg_scr_lower, igg_scr_upper)
```
